question: Will more sanctions stop the sabotage, yes or no?

lines.text: Estonia says Russia ordered an arson attack on a defence company in Tallinn.
The target was Milrem Robotics, which supplies robot vehicles to Ukraine's army.
Prime Minister Kristen Michal called it an act of sabotage commissioned by Russian special services.

scene.quote: An act of sabotage commissioned by Russian special services

lines.text: The fire broke out on the night of the fifteenth of August.
Firefighters put it out quickly, and no one's life was in danger.
Within three days, three suspects were detained.
Latvia handed all three over to Estonia on the seventeenth and eighteenth of September.
Searches turned up fire-setting materials and data storage devices.
The security service chief says it was the first successful attack in Estonia this year.

scene.quote: The first successful attack in Estonia this year

lines.text: The service says it has prevented the vast majority of attacks.

scene.quote: We have prevented the vast majority of attacks

lines.text: The Kremlin denies it. Spokesman Dmitry Peskov says such statements are baseless.
Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna says the answer will be more sanctions and more support for Ukraine.
A fire in Tallinn, now blamed on Moscow. Will more sanctions stop the sabotage, yes or no?
